The only refundable items on the non-metered branch would be un-published add-ons or ERP/toll overcharges [RD-2]; the record shows no such item (waiting $0.00, discount $0.00) [F6], and no tolls data exists for this trip, so nothing is refundable.

The single off-route segment 21:25–21:32 (4.46 km driven vs 2.34 km optimal, +2.12 km) [F3] is the subject of the RD-1 review. It is not excused by RD-4(a): no traffic incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F14], and a speed-band record alone cannot exempt a segment [F11][RD-4]. The driver asked before the diversion, at 21:21: "Traffic ahead on Central Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5?" [F7], and the rider replied at 21:22: "Sure, no problem." [F8]. The rider's message is timestamped and precedes the segment start of 21:25 by several minutes [F3][F9], and the chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) [F9], so it is a valid consent in the rider's own words — not merely the driver's after-the-fact claim [F10][RD-5]. The record therefore ties the segment to the named road, so the agreed diversion to AMK Ave 5 is covered and the segment is exempt; it is not a driver's own errand away from the agreed route [F13][RD-5].

On the trace's RD-4 screen the segment is not exempt via traffic incidents (✗) [F14], but the RD-5 rider-agreement branch does exempt it, so the RD-1 obligation is met and there is no unexempted deviation. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows route disputes upheld in the last 90 days = 0 [F17], so no account flag arises [RD-6]. Since the fare is a fixed quote and the deviation is excused, the trace's allowed outcome no_action follows.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Good news — this one's closed with no refund due, but you haven't lost anything.

Your trip was a RydeX fixed-quote booking. You were quoted $36.95 up front, and on a fixed quote your price doesn't change if the driver covers extra kilometres. The extra distance on your trip was also on a diversion you agreed to before it happened, in your own messages.

So the fare stays as charged, and there's nothing to pay back or deduct. No refund applies here, and nothing changes on your account. Thanks for flagging it — questions are always welcome.

DRIVER: Good news — this dispute is closed in your favour, with no action against you.

The fare was a RydeX fixed quote of $36.95, so the extra 2.12 km didn't change what the rider paid, and no refund was due on the fare. The off-route stretch was also covered by the rider's own agreement to the diversion, made in the chat before you set off on it.

No amount is owed either way, and no flag has been placed on your account — your record showed no upheld route disputes in the last 90 days. Keep driving as usual.

Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts.
